fault_types.damper: OA damper stuck at a fixed position
fault_types.valve_leak: cooling-coil valve leaks (10% of travel) when commanded closed

default.description: fault-free + 4 stuck-damper runs + the single valve-leak run (coi_leakage_010; the LBNL benchmark's SDAHU set) and a spliced fault-onset run

quirks.note: In every faulted run SA_SPSPT is a constant -400.25 (a placeholder, not a setpoint); masked to missing.

In the fault-free run SA_SP is not a measured static pressure: it holds ~402-403 (the ~1.61 inH2O setpoint in Pa) with the fan off as well as on; masked to missing. In the faulted runs SA_SP is the measured static in inH2O and is kept.
SA_CFM and RA_CFM are published as cfm x 60 (ft3/h); divided by 60 to cfm before mapping.

known_issues: Valve and damper signals are 0-1 fractions; they are rescaled to percent.
Valves and dampers map to the controller demand columns (*_DM), not the measured positions: a stuck device's position hides the fault the rules look for.

The unit exports no fan run-status point (SF_SPD_DM, which the inventory lists as the supply-fan status, equals SYS_CTL in every row). CAMBER derives one: SF_ON = 1 when the speed command SF_CS is above 0, which agrees with the supply-fan power being above 5 W in 99.8% of rows; it maps to supply_fan_status, SF_CS to supply_fan_speed.

The unit's minimum OA is a fixed 10% damper position (inventory section 1.2), which measures as a 1.6% OA fraction (median of 119,163 occupied, fan-on minutes at that position): the run template sets min_oa_pct 1.6. A damper stuck at 10% is therefore indistinguishable from normal operation outside economizer weather; its symptom is the missed economizer (61.8% vs 1.6% OA in 33.8-60 F weather).

The economizer runs only between 33.8 F and 60 F (inventory section 1.2): below 33.8 F it is locked out by design, so cold-weather 'missed free cooling' is not a fault on this unit. The run template sets economizer_high_limit's high_limit_f to 60.
damper_stuck_100 is a short run (2018-04-01 to 2018-11-01).

data_issues.title: The simulated calendar runs one weekday late and follows DST

default.description: fault-free + 3 OA-damper runs (the LBNL benchmark's FCU set)

known_issues: Valves and dampers map to the controller demand columns (*_DM).
Timestamps are month-first (MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM); the ingester pins that format.

The design minimum is a 30% damper position (inventory section 1.2), which measures as a 10.5% OA fraction on the fault-free run (occupied, fan-on minutes); the run template's min_oa_pct 10 matches it.

FCU_SPD is the 3-speed fan's speed in rev/s (0 / 9.75 / 13.08), not a percent, and is not mapped; CAMBER derives the fan status FCU_ON = (FCU_DA_CFM > 10 cfm), which matches FCU_SPD > 0 in every row. FCU_CTRL (0 shutdown / 1 operate / 2 setback) maps to occupancy with setback read as unoccupied.

The OA-damper leak runs are a narrow test of the OA-fraction threshold: 20 / 50 / 80% leakage give 12.7 / 15.4 / 17.4% OA against the rule's 15% (10% minimum + 5%) excess line, so the leak-50 detection rests on a 0.4-point margin.
outdoor_air_fraction targets both the stuck/leaking damper runs and the OA-inlet blockage run (0.7% OA), which is under-ventilation by the same physics.

data_issues.title: The damper 'stuck at 30%' run is the unit's normal minimum
data_issues.evidence: The unit's minimum OA damper position is 30%, which is also the fault-free position in 174,453 occupied, fan-on minutes. In OADMPRStuck_30 the occupied fan-on OA fraction is 10.53% (temperature balance) / 10.54% (OA_CFM / supply flow), identical to the fault-free run's 10.53% / 10.54%; the two differ only in unoccupied setback minutes with the fan cycling (10.5% vs 0.2%).

fault_types.terminal_damper: hot- or cold-deck terminal damper stuck

default.description: fault-free + 2 stuck-OA-damper runs (the LBNL benchmark's set)

known_issues: Each run's CSV is ~300 MB uncompressed; the full subset extracts ~17 GB.
Timestamps are month-first (MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM); the ingester pins that format.

The minimum OA is seasonal (inventory section 1.2(ii)): a 28% damper position Jun-Aug and 45% otherwise, which measure as 11.9% and 31.8% OA (median OA_CFM / supply flow over the occupied, fan-on minutes of the fault-free run at those positions: 30,014 and 37,059 minutes). By design the hot deck heats to 90 F while the cold deck cools to 55 F: both coil valves are open in 26% of occupied fan-on minutes of the fault-free run, so simultaneous_heat_cool is not run on this unit.

SYS_CTL is 0 shutdown / 1 operate / 2 setback; it maps to occupancy with setback read as unoccupied. CSF_CS (equal to HSF_CS in every row) is the fan status; OA_CFM is the measured OA flow and CSA_CFM + HSA_CFM the supply flow.

default.description: parallel-FPU fault-free + 2 stuck-damper + a stuck and a leaking reheat valve

known_issues: Faults are imposed on the SOUTH zone box (_S columns); the other zones stay healthy (see the data issues).
The reheat valve maps to the demand column (RH_VLV_DM_S); VAV_DMPR_S has no demand twin and is the measured position.
The room setpoints RMCLGSPT_S / RMHTGSPT_S (72 / 68 F occupied, 85 / 55 F unoccupied) map to cool_sp / heat_sp, so unmet_setpoint_hours evaluates.

SA_TEMP is the AHU supply air entering the box and maps to mixed_air_temp, the role CAMBER uses for a terminal's entering primary air. In a parallel box the reheat coil sees that primary air plus the plenum air the box fan adds when it runs, so SA_TEMP is a proxy for the coil's entering air, not a measurement of it.

reheat_minimization_g36 is not run: VAV_PM_CFM_SP_S is the active airflow setpoint (the rule reads it as the design maximum and cannot fire on the fault-free run), and G36's dual-maximum reheat logic applies to single-duct VAV boxes, not fan-powered ones.

On the series (SFPU) boxes airflow_tracking also fires on six of the ten reheat-valve leak / stuck runs (an overheated room drives the primary-airflow command up); on the parallel (PFPU) boxes it fires on exactly the stuck-damper and airflow-sensor-bias runs.
Scenario ids replace '%' with 'pct', '+' with 'p' and a leading '-' with 'm'.

quirks.note: The exported outdoor dry-bulb (OA_TEMP) and wet-bulb (OA_TEMP_WB) columns are swapped relative to the dataset inventory; swapped back before mapping.
The secondary chilled-water loop's supply and return temperatures are swapped; swapped back before mapping (the primary loop is correct).

The simulated chiller/tower design curves are not published: calibrate the chiller_efficiency / cooling_tower_approach design ceilings from the fault-free run.
Water-side only: the refrigerant-side chiller drift detectors cannot run on it.
The tower-fouling severities are heat-transfer multipliers: 065 is the most severe, 095 the mildest (x 0.95, which no rule sees).

data_issues.title: Outdoor dry-bulb and wet-bulb columns are swapped
data_issues.evidence: Two independent checks. The tower leaving-water setpoint follows max(wet-bulb + 8 F, 60 F): on the 210,661 minutes above the 60 F floor CT_SW_TEMPSPT equals OA_TEMP + 8 to a median 0.28 F but OA_TEMP_WB + 8 only to 6.27 F. The chilled-water reset follows the outdoor dry-bulb: CWL_PRI_SW_TEMPSPT matches the reset of OA_TEMP_WB with a p90 error of 0.49 F (hourly), and the reset of OA_TEMP only to 4.54 F. OA_TEMP_WB also exceeds OA_TEMP in 99.3% of rows, which a wet-bulb cannot do.

contradicts.document: Chiller-plant inventory Table 2 (OA_TEMP: dry bulb; OA_TEMP_WB: wet bulb), Eq. 3 / Table 1 (tower setpoint = wet-bulb + 8 F) and Eq. 2 (the chilled-water reset follows the dry-bulb)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Swapped back before mapping (swap quirk), in every run.

data_issues.title: Secondary-loop supply and return temperatures are swapped
data_issues.evidence: In the 169,809 rows where the secondary loop carries load (CWL_SEC_LOAD > 10) the labelled return is colder than the labelled supply in 100% of rows, while the primary loop's return is warmer in 99.9% of them; hourly (supply - return) correlates +0.88 with CWL_SEC_LOAD.

contradicts.document: Chiller-plant inventory Table 2 (CWL_SEC_SW_TEMP: supply, CWL_SEC_RW_TEMP: return water temperature)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Swapped back before mapping (swap quirk), in every run; the primary loop is left as published.

data_issues.title: The chilled-water reset spans 44-54 F, not 42-52 F
data_issues.evidence: CWL_PRI_SW_TEMPSPT ranges 44.0-54.0 F (54.0 in 327,603 rows, 44.0 in 36,899). Eq. 2 with 44 / 54 F bounds reproduces it from the true dry-bulb to a median 0.00 F (p90 0.49 F, hourly); with the inventory's 42 / 52 F bounds the median error is 2.00 F.

contradicts.document: Chiller-plant inventory Eq. 2 (chilled-water setpoint reset between 42 F and 52 F over 60-80 F outdoor dry-bulb)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Left as published; the setpoint is not mapped to a role, and nothing in CAMBER assumes the 42-52 F range.

contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.evidence: The archive has ChillerPlant_chiller_fouling_065.csv and _095.csv, which Tables 3-4 do not list. Against the fault-free run chiller 1's annual energy rises 61% (065) and 6.3% (095); chiller 2's falls 3.5% / rises 0.2%.

contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

why a Brick On_Off_Status on a boiler is an enable, not proof of firing
a detection gap: boiler fouling is invisible to temperature-only rules
datasets.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (with PNNL, NREL, ORNL and Drexel University)
datasets.citation: Granderson, J., Lin, G., Chen, Y., Casillas, A., Im, P., Jung, S., Benne, K., Ling, J., Gorthala, R., Wen, J., Chen, Z., Huang, S., Vrabie, D. (2022). LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. doi:10.25984/1881324

default.description: fault-free + fouling + PI mistuning + a temperature sensor bias

quirks.note: BOI_STA_1/BOI_STA_2 are the boiler enable, not burner firing, so they are left unmapped; rules needing boiler_status decline on this plant.

known_issues: The boiler status points are enables (see the data issues); boiler_status is not mapped.

BOI_GAS_CSUM_1 / _2 are the boilers' instantaneous gas input in kW (Table 2), not cumulative counters: 26% of consecutive steps fall and the value is 0 in 50.5% of rows. CAMBER has no gas-input role yet, so the gas-per-heat signature of boiler fouling (boiler 1's annual gas +57% / +26% / +5.5% at 065 / 080 / 095) has no detector; nor is there a supply-temperature-vs-setpoint check (the plant exports no supply-temperature setpoint; Table 1 fixes it at 176 F). Both are follow-ups: hw_pump_dp_reset, the template's one rule, detects none of the 16 faults.
PM_POW_1 / PM_POW_2 are the literal string 'NAN' in the eight runs the inventory's Table 4 marks with an asterisk.

data_issues.title: BOI_STA is the boiler enable, not burner firing
data_issues.evidence: In the fault-free run BOI_STA_1 is 1 in 100% of rows while boiler 1 burns no gas (BOI_GAS_CSUM_1 = 0) in 50.5% of them.

data_issues.evidence: HWL_DPSPT is the constant 480.52 in every row: 17.36 psi expressed in inH2O, matching Table 1's 17.5 psi loop differential-pressure setpoint and the fault-free HWL_DP median (480.52).

data_issues.title: Pump 2's power has negative spikes in the fault-free run
data_issues.evidence: Fault-free PM_POW_2 reaches -102,400.7 kW (2018-12-15 11:19, pump 2 off); 40 rows are below -1 kW and 13 below -1,000 kW. (The literal 'NAN' pump-power entries in eight runs are documented by the inventory's Table 4 footnote.)

data_issues.title: hot_water_temp_bias biases the loop return, not the supply
data_issues.evidence: In the four hot_water_temp_bias runs HWL_RW_TEMP moves by -7.2 / -3.6 / +3.6 / +7.2 F (median difference from the fault-free run for -4 / -2 / +2 / +4 C) and HWL_SW_TEMP by 0.0.

contradicts.document: Boiler-plant inventory Tables 3-4 (bias of the hot water leaving temperature sensor of the hot water loop)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.title: The boiler and loop-DP bias faults are hidden in their own sensors
data_issues.evidence: The controlled sensors keep reading their setpoints: in the boiler_bias runs BOI_SW_TEMP_1 stays at 176 F while the loop supply HWL_SW_TEMP moves by +7.2 / +3.6 / -3.6 / -7.2 F (-4 / -2 / +2 / +4 C); in the hot_water_pressure_bias runs HWL_DP stays at its setpoint (median difference 0.0) and pump 1's speed moves by +0.034 / +0.016 / -0.013 / -0.025 (-20 / -10 / +10 / +20%).

contradicts.document: Boiler-plant inventory section 3 (for sensor bias faults the logged value of the faulty sensor is the faulty value)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

datasets.title: Building Data Genome 2 (whole-building meters)
datasets.summary: 3,053 hourly whole-building energy meters from 1,636 non-residential buildings on 19 sites, 2016-2017: electricity, chilled water, steam, hot water, gas, water, irrigation and solar, with site weather and building metadata.
teaches: change-point M&V baselines (ASHRAE Guideline 14 acceptance)
weather normalization with the site's own weather station
portfolio storage: one facility per site, one equipment per building meter
datasets.publisher: Building and Urban Data Science (BUDS) Lab, National University of Singapore
datasets.citation: Miller, C., Kathirgamanathan, A., Picchetti, B. et al. (2020). The Building Data Genome Project 2, energy meter data from the ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III competition. Scientific Data 7, 368. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00712-x
datasets.timezone: naive timestamps on one uniform hourly grid: no daylight-saving gap or repeated hour at any site. metadata.csv gives each site's IANA zone and the publisher describes the timestamps as local time, but one site's meters run about 4-5 h behind its weather (see the data issues).

default.description: metadata + weather + cleaned electricity and chilled-water meters for up to 4 buildings on each of 10 sites (plus the buildings the M&V example uses)

full.description: all 19 files (raw, cleaned and the competition subset); ingest reads every site and every cleaned meter

known_issues: Licence is CC-BY-SA 4.0 (the repository LICENSE): analysis and commercial use are fine; a redistributed adaptation of the data must keep the same licence.
Meter readings are hourly energy per interval; they are stored as an hourly-mean rate (numerically equal), electricity under 'power' and the other meters under 'energy_rate'.
One facility per site (ds-bdg2-<site>); each building meter is an equipment '<building>__<meter>' of class '<METER>_METER'. Weather (airTemperature, degC) is converted to F on equipment 'weather'.

The catalog ingests the publisher's cleaned meters. The raw electricity and chilled-water files carry ~24,700 all-zero building-days each in 2016 (meter outages); the cleaned electricity has none, and the cleaned chilled water keeps ~25,000 zero days (plants that do not run).

1-5% of building-days are partial (fewer than 23 hourly readings): 2.2% of cleaned electricity days and 4.8% of cleaned chilled-water days in 2016. Summing them as whole days biases daily models; the benchmark fits whole days only.
kaggle/kaggle.csv (the competition subset, numeric building ids) is downloaded by the full subset but not ingested; it is known to mix units across sites.

data_issues.title: One site's chilled water is about 1,000x too large
data_issues.evidence: The 87 Eagle chilled-water meters have a median 2016 intensity of 17,417 kWh/ft2/yr (cleaned; 17,913 raw) and a median 1,389x the same building's electricity; the other sites' chilled-water meters have a per-building median of 45.8 kWh/ft2/yr and no site median above 77.5. Divided by 1,000 Eagle's median is 17.4 kWh/ft2/yr, 1.4x its electricity -- the factor a kBTU series converted as mmBTU (the unit Table 4 lists for Eagle's chilled water) would carry.

contradicts.document: Miller et al. 2020, Table 4 (Eagle chilled water in mmBTU) and Usage Notes (unit-conversion mistakes fixed in the raw and cleaned sets)

data_issues.handling_note: Ingested as published (no rescale: the factor is inferred, not documented). Kept out of the benchmark's EUI rollup, which is electricity-only; the change-point acceptance and residual-autocorrelation metrics are scale-free.

data_issues.title: One site's meter timestamps lag its weather by about 4-5 hours
data_issues.evidence: Eagle's weekday electricity profile runs ~5 h later than the pooled profile of the other sites (overnight minimum at 07-08 h vs 03 h; daytime plateau 14-19 h vs 10-15 h) while its air temperature peaks at 15 h like every site's, and its chilled water peaks at 20 h (12-17 h elsewhere). Cross-correlated with its own air temperature, Eagle's meters align best when the weather is shifted 5 h (chilled water) / 3 h (electricity) later, against -4 to +1 h at the other sites (where the correlation is meaningful) -- a UTC-like clock on a US/Eastern site.

contradicts.document: Miller et al. 2020, Usage Notes (the BDG2 timestamps, weather included, are in the local time zone)

data_issues.handling_note: Left as published: the offset is inferred (4 or 5 h), not documented, so it is not shifted. Daily models are barely affected; an hourly or time-of-week analysis of Eagle should shift its meters.

datasets.title: LBNL Building 59: three years of a real office's rooftop units, zone CO2 and underfloor terminals
datasets.summary: A real two-floor office in Berkeley, California (2018-2020, 1-minute BAS trends): four 20,000 cfm rooftop units with measured outdoor-air flow (from April 2020) and OA-damper position, 11 zone CO2 sensors, 51 underfloor fan-powered terminals with reheat, site weather and a Brick model. The building has no DCV; its record includes wildfire smoke-mode damper closures, the 2020 shelter-in-place occupancy drop and real sensor faults.
teaches: DCV verification on a building without DCV: the honest answer is 'not judged', never a false 'functioning'
joining zone CO2 to the air handler that brings in outdoor air (served-by grouping from a Brick model)
sensor health on real faults: a return-air point that copies supply air, gap-filled OA flow, inaccurate mixed-air sensors
timestamps published in UTC: moving a dataset onto the site's wall clock
datasets.citation: Luo, N., Wang, Z., Blum, D., Weyandt, C., Bourassa, N., Piette, M.A., Hong, T. (2022). A three-year dataset supporting research on building energy management and occupancy analytics. Scientific Data 9, 156. doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01257-x. Data: Hong, T., Luo, N., Blum, D., Wang, Z. (2022). A three-year building operational performance dataset for informing energy efficiency. Dryad. doi:10.7941/D1N33Q
datasets.manual_instructions: Dryad serves these files only to a browser (its file API needs a bearer token and its download links sit behind a bot check). Open https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.7941/D1N33Q, download Building_59.zip and README_Dryad_Bldg59.txt (the full subset also needs data_description_table_3year_clean_data.xlsx and metadata_Dryad_Bldg59.docx) into one directory, then run `camber datasets ingest lbnl-b59 --from-dir <that directory> --store <store>`; the files are checked against the sizes and SHA-256 digests Dryad itself publishes.
datasets.equipment: 4 rooftop units (AHU), 11 zone CO2 sensors and 51 underfloor fan terminals (VAV) grouped to their RTU by the Brick model, site weather
datasets.timezone: published in UTC (undocumented; see the data issues) and converted at ingest to America/Los_Angeles wall-clock time; 1-minute RTU and zone data, 15-minute weather; 2018-01-01 to 2020-12-31 with a few multi-day gaps; zone CO2 from 2019-08-19 (none in February-March 2020)

default.description: the four RTUs, the 11 CO2 zones and site weather, all three years

full.description: adds the 51 underfloor fan terminals (zone temperature, setpoints, reheat valve, fan speed) and the documentation files

quirks.note: RTU outdoor-air flow before 2020-04-10 22:00 UTC is the publisher's gap fill (the four units move as one, r = 0.998-0.999), not a measurement; masked.
RTU04's return-air temperature is a copy of its supply-air temperature from 2019-09-19 (99.1% identical in 2020); left in place for the sensor-health copied-signal check.
Mixed-air temperatures leave the OA/RA band in up to 23% of hours (RTU01, H2 2019); left in place.
Measured OA flow saturates at 19,999 cfm and exceeds the unit's supply flow in 1-7% of hours after 2020-04-10; left in place.
zone_022_co2 reads below outdoor air (27,120 minutes < 350 ppm, 11,661 at exactly 72 ppm); left in place.
Fan-speed feedback reads -25% while the fan is stopped (0.9% of minutes); left in place.
Zone -> RTU assignment follows the Brick model, which disagrees with Table 1 of the data descriptor for every CO2 zone.
Brick point names differ from the CSV columns for the OA flow and damper, and five RTU points are missing from the model; the mapping file overrides the Brick grouping for those 20 columns.

known_issues: Licence: Dryad lists the data as CC0-1.0, but the metadata JSON inside the archive states CC BY 4.0 (DataGovernance/Sharing/License) and the data descriptor is CC BY 4.0. The catalog applies the stricter CC-BY-4.0 and asks for attribution.
Download is manual (see the manual instructions): the pinned sha256s equal the sha-256 digests Dryad publishes for each file.

The RTUs are grouped by the dataset's Brick model (RTU01-RTU04 own their supply, return and mixed-air temperatures and supply-fan speed); the mapping file adds the 20 RTU columns the model misnames or lacks. The 11 CO2 zones and 51 terminals are placed by name (RTU0N_zone_<z>, RTU0N_uft_<z>) from the model's zone -> RTU location, which the owner grouping does not follow.

The published CSVs are the publisher's cleaned version: gaps were filled by linear interpolation, KNN or matrix factorization depending on gap length (README; descriptor Table 3). Only the outdoor-air flow, whose raw record starts in April 2020, is masked by CAMBER; other long fills (e.g. zone CO2 gaps) remain.

Documented events (descriptor Table 2, local dates): wildfire smoke mode 2018-11-12 to 11-20 and 2020-08-24 to 09-06 (OA dampers held at their 10% minimum), shelter-in-place from 2020-03-18 (zone CO2 barely rises above outdoor for the rest of 2020), and MPC tests on 21 days in October-December 2020.

The building has no DCV and the RTU supply fans run 24/7 at one common speed; there is no economizer command point, so the DCV rules infer the economizer from OAT and mostly decline in Berkeley's mild climate.
Camera occupancy counts (occ.csv, May 2018 - Feb 2019) and Wi-Fi counts (wifi.csv) are floor-level, and neither overlaps the CO2 record in a usable way; they are not mapped.

Per-RTU floor areas and design populations are not published (two office floors of 2,325 m2 each), so the ASHRAE 62.1 VRP is not run per RTU; see issue #17 for the system-level procedure this dataset could validate.
34 duplicated timestamps in rtu_sa_t.csv (February 2020) are dropped (the first reading is kept).

Ingest cost (measured): the default subset extracts 644 MB and ingests in about 15 s; the full subset extracts 2.0 GB, ingests in about 75 s and peaks near 7 GB of memory, because the five 1-minute terminal tables (51 zones each) are held while their 51 runs are split out.

data_issues.title: Timestamps are UTC, which no document states
data_issues.evidence: Solar radiation at the campus station peaks at 20:00-21:00 (792-817 W/m2, 15-25 June 2019) and is zero from 04:00 to 12:00; the camera occupancy counts peak at 17:00-22:00 on weekdays (25 people at 17:00 vs 0.1 at 11:00); and the RTU files run straight through the US spring-forward hour (71 rows from 01:55 to 03:05 on 2018-03-11, 2019-03-10 and 2020-03-08) with no repeated hour in November. Solar noon in Berkeley is about 20:10 UTC in June, so the stamps are UTC (Pacific time minus 7-8 h).

contradicts.document: README_Dryad_Bldg59.txt and the data description table give no time zone; the data descriptor presents the building's schedules and the Table 2 event dates as local time

data_issues.handling_note: Not a correction of values: the ingest declares source_timezone UTC and local_timezone America/Los_Angeles (CAMBER's timestamp semantics, applied in every mode), so the store holds Berkeley wall-clock time and the occupied-hour schedules line up. The November fall-back hour keeps both readings (averaged); quirk timestamps below are UTC.

data_issues.title: RTU outdoor-air flow before 2020-04-10 is imputed, not measured
data_issues.evidence: Up to 2020-04-10 21:59 UTC the hourly OA flows of the four RTUs correlate 0.998-0.999 pairwise (one pattern scaled four ways, 1,005,495 minute rows per RTU); from 22:00 UTC on they correlate 0.72-0.83, the daily minimum drops from above 2,590 cfm to 1,305-1,730 cfm, and the readings reach the transmitter ceiling of 19,999 cfm, which the earlier values never exceed (maxima 13,093-16,148 cfm).

contradicts.document: Data description table (rtu_oa_fr.csv: available Apr-Dec 2020) versus the file, which has values for all of 2018-2020; README methods (gaps filled by linear interpolation, KNN and matrix factorization)

data_issues.handling_note: Masked (NaN) before 2020-04-10 22:00 UTC in every RTU run, so no OA-flow rule or check judges the imputed years; the OA damper position is kept for the whole period.

data_issues.title: RTU04's return-air temperature is a copy of its supply-air temperature from September 2019
data_issues.evidence: rtu_004_ra_temp equals rtu_004_sa_temp to the last digit in 0.04% of 2018 minutes, 29.8% of 2019 and 99.1% of 2020; from 2019-09-19 on 98.5% of days are at least 90% identical. The other three RTUs' return and supply agree in 0.13-0.22% of minutes (median difference 4.2-5.2 F).

contradicts.document: Brick model (rtu_004_ra_temp is a Return_Air_Temperature_Sensor of RTU04) and the data description table (Roof Top Unit return air temperature)

data_issues.handling_note: Left in place on purpose: it is a genuine data fault that the sensor-health layer's copied-signal check (camber.sensorhealth.copied_signal_consistency) should find. Economizer and mixing-balance results on RTU04 after 2019-09-19 judge a copy.

data_issues.title: Mixed-air temperatures leave the outdoor/return band, mostly in 2018-2019
data_issues.evidence: Hourly mixed-air temperature lies more than 2 F outside [min(OAT, RAT), max(OAT, RAT)] -- which a blend of the two cannot do -- in 10.7% (Jul-Dec 2018), 23.0% (Jul-Dec 2019) and 0.6% (Jul-Dec 2020) of RTU01 hours and 4.2%, 9.2% and 13.5% of RTU04 hours (RTU04's return is a copy of supply from 2019-09, see above); RTU02 and RTU03 stay at or below 3.6%.

contradicts.document: Data description table (rtu_*_ma_temp: Roof Top Unit mixed air temperature; the only outlier criterion is < 32 F or > 122 F)

data_issues.handling_note: Left in place: an inaccurate mixed-air sensor is a real sensor-health test (camber.sensorhealth.mixing_consistency; issue #16 would weigh the flow balance into the trust score). Rules that read MAT on RTU01/RTU04 in 2018-2019 are judging a doubtful sensor.

data_issues.title: Measured OA flow sits at a 19,999 cfm ceiling and above the unit's own supply flow
data_issues.evidence: After 2020-04-10 the OA flow reads exactly 19,999 cfm in 5.55% of RTU04 minutes and 1.24% of RTU01 minutes, and exceeds the same unit's filtered supply airflow in 7.3% (RTU04), 4.1% (RTU01), 1.5% (RTU03) and 1.3% (RTU02) of hours. The descriptor gives each RTU a design supply airflow of 20,000 cfm and a minimum OA of 5,000 cfm.

contradicts.document: Data descriptor, HVAC system description (design airflow 20,000 cfm per RTU, minimum outdoor air 5,000 cfm)

data_issues.handling_note: Left in place: the ceiling is the transmitter span, and OA above supply is a flow-station error the DCV rule's floor check is not affected by (it looks at low flows). Treat OA flow above the supply flow as unmeasured.

data_issues.title: One zone CO2 sensor reads far below outdoor air, and every sensor carries a 72 ppm floor
data_issues.evidence: zone_022_co2 is below 350 ppm in 27,120 minutes (8,420 of them in June 2020, when its monthly median is 362 ppm against 409-420 ppm for the other ten zones) and reads exactly 72 ppm in 11,661 minutes; the other ten sensors touch that same 72 ppm value 1-5 times each. Outdoor CO2 was about 410 ppm.

contradicts.document: Data description table (zone_*_co2: CO2 concentration; the only outlier criterion is < 0)

data_issues.handling_note: Left in place: dcv_system_verification drops CO2 outside 250-5,000 ppm and excludes a zone whose CO2 stays implausible, and sensor health's zone-vs-outdoor CO2 check flags it.

data_issues.title: Fan-speed feedback reads -25% while the fans are stopped
data_issues.evidence: Each supply- and return-fan speed feedback reads -24.9% or -25.0% in 0.9% of minutes (12,419 minutes for RTU01's supply fan, in 13 episodes, e.g. 2018-01-29 and 2019-02-26); in those minutes the unit's filtered supply airflow has a median of 0 cfm.

contradicts.document: Data description table (rtu_*_sf_vfd_spd_fbk_tn: supply fan speed in %)

data_issues.title: The Brick model and the descriptor's Table 1 assign the zones to different RTUs

datasets.title: Finnish laboratory office room with occupancy-based DCV (ground-truth counts)
datasets.summary: One 22 m3 laboratory office room (up to 4 people) ventilated with outdoor air by a VAV supply, at 1-minute resolution: room CO2, supply and extract airflow, supply- and exhaust-air CO2, temperature and ground-truth occupant counts. Two training sets under assorted ventilation strategies (about 5.9 and 2.8 days, non-contiguous) and a 24-hour test in which the airflow followed an occupancy-count DCV law (base flow plus 6 l/s per estimated occupant).
teaches: what a working DCV looks like: outdoor air rising with occupancy and CO2
checking a documented control law against the trend (base 3 l/s + 6 l/s per person)
occupant counts as the occupied signal (count > 0) instead of a schedule
datasets.publisher: Aalto University and Metropolia University of Applied Sciences
datasets.citation: Mikala, J., Xu, Y., Huotari, M. (2026). Indoor occupancy ground truth dataset with variable ventilation (version 1.0). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.18299691
datasets.equipment: one office room: VAV outdoor-air supply (and equal extract), room CO2, supply/exhaust CO2, ground-truth occupant count
datasets.timezone: naive timestamps, time zone not documented (taken as local lab time); 1-minute samples; each file is a set of non-contiguous days (training 1: 38 days from 2024-02-28 to 2025-03-25; training 2: 12 days in October-November 2025; test: 2025-11-24, 25 and 27)

quirks.note: Supply airflow reads slightly negative with the supply stopped and spikes to 362 l/s in training 1; left in place.

known_issues: The ventilation test controlled the airflow on the ML occupant estimate, not the ground-truth count; the two agree in 74.7% of test minutes. CAMBER maps the ground-truth count as occupancy.
The training sets used 'multiple ventilation control strategies' (not described), so a DCV verdict on them describes that mix, not a DCV law.
Every file is a set of separate days, not a continuous record: no drift, schedule or M&V analysis applies.
The room was renovated (wall insulation added) after March 2025, between training 1 and training 2.
The time zone is not documented; occupancy falls between 05:00 and 18:00 in all three files, consistent with local time.

data_issues.title: The test's DCV law runs at 4 l/s + 6 l/s per person, not the documented 3 l/s base
data_issues.evidence: In ventilation_test.csv the median supply airflow is 4.04, 10.06, 15.93 and 22.01 l/s at 0, 1, 2 and 3 estimated occupants -- 4 + 6n -- and the median residual against 3 + 6n is +1.02 l/s over the 1,430 minutes (median absolute residual 1.09 l/s; 76% of minutes within 1.5 l/s once the 5-minute update lag is allowed for). A +1 l/s offset at 4 l/s is 25%, beyond the flow sensor's stated +/-5%.

contradicts.document: Zenodo record description, 'Occupancy-based control': base ventilation 3 l/s (unoccupied), 6 l/s per detected occupant, updated every 5 minutes
contradicts.citation: Mikala, Xu, Huotari 2026, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.18299691

data_issues.handling_note: Nothing is changed: CAMBER's DCV rule does not assume a control law, it tests whether outdoor air rises with demand. The template's area floor (Ra x Az) sits below both 3 and 4 l/s.

data_issues.title: Supply airflow reads negative near zero flow and spikes above 100 l/s
data_issues.evidence: The supply airflow is negative in 52, 47 and 14 minutes of the three files (minimum -6.40 l/s in training 1), and above 100 l/s in 63 minutes of training 1 (maximum 362.4 l/s on 2024-09-06, 2024-09-19 and 2025-03-25) -- about 59 air changes per hour in the 22 m3 room, against a test-period maximum of 64.9 l/s.

datasets.title: Brains4Buildings Windesheim office rooms: two CO2 sensors, ventilation valve and occupancy
datasets.summary: Three office rooms at Windesheim University of Applied Sciences (Zwolle, NL) for 3-4 weeks in October-November 2022, 15-minute preprocessed data: the BMS room CO2 sensor and a desk-mounted SCD41 CO2 sensor, the ventilation valve opening as a fraction of the room's maximum flow, PIR presence, a people counter, Bluetooth phone counts and outdoor weather, with room volumes and maximum flows.
teaches: a valve that follows both a clock and CO2: what a DCV verdict can and cannot separate
how much a DCV verdict depends on which CO2 sensor you trust (BMS vs desk SCD41)
declining honestly when the OA signal is an assumption, not a measurement
datasets.publisher: Research Group Energy Transition, Windesheim University of Applied Sciences
datasets.citation: ter Hofte, H., van Ravenzwaaij, N., Nijboer, E. (2023). Brains4Buildings2022 dataset: CO2 concentration, ventilation flow rate and occupancy of 3 office rooms at Windesheim University of Applied Sciences. https://github.com/energietransitie/b4b-windesheim-brains4buildings2022-dataset (commit 188573d)
datasets.equipment: 3 office rooms (VAV-class equipment ROOM_<id>), two of them also with the SCD41 CO2 sensor as equipment ROOM_<id>_scd41
datasets.timezone: ISO timestamps with UTC offsets (Europe/Amsterdam, crossing the 2022-10-30 DST change), converted at ingest to Amsterdam wall-clock time; 15-minute intervals (start of interval), 2022-10-06/10 to 2022-11-02

default.description: the preprocessed file, room metadata and README (1.2 MB)

full.description: the preprocessed file, room metadata and README (1.2 MB); the raw measurement files are not ingested

quirks.note: CO2 values were shifted by the publisher so each sensor's minimum reads 416 ppm (baseline correction); left as published.

known_issues: The valve fraction is a position (0.20 at the valve's mechanical minimum, 1.00 open) of a constant-pressure system, not a measured flow; the DCV rule judges OA from it with a caveat. Rooms 917810 and 999169 have a maximum flow of 240 m3/h (room metadata), so 0.20 is about 48 m3/h.

In rooms 917810 and 999169 the valve follows the clock (mean opening 0.51-0.71 at 07:00-10:00 on weekdays, 0.20 all weekend except a 03:00-05:00 bump) and also CO2: within the same weekday hour it correlates 0.53/0.61 with the BMS CO2 and 0.47/0.73 with the desk SCD41, and it is above 0.25 in 100%/68% of weekday intervals with BMS CO2 above 800 ppm (14-15% below 500 ppm). The DCV rule's median CO2 lift mixes the scheduled openings in and reads 'OA modulates, but not with demand' on the BMS sensor, 'functioning' on room 999169's SCD41.

The catalog ingests the publisher's preprocessed file (duplicates removed, CO2 below 5 ppm removed, CO2 baseline shifted, 15-minute interpolation without bridging gaps of 90 minutes or more); the raw measurement files are downloadable from the repository but not ingested.

The Xovis people counter covers about 40% of intervals in rooms 917810 and 999169 and 3% in 925038; the Bluetooth phone counts see only registered phones. Neither is the occupancy CAMBER maps where a PIR exists.
3-4 weeks of data per room: too short for drift or seasonal analyses.
The publisher mints no DOI; the catalog pins the repository commit instead.
